title: Distinct GCDs (Hard Version)
statementMd:
**This is the hard version of the problem. The difference between the versions is that in this version, $n \leq 5000$. You can hack only if you solved all versions of this problem.**

*Legend has it that when Gauss was a young schoolboy, his teacher tasked the class with summing the integers from $1$ to $100$, likely as a way to keep them occupied for a while. However, young Gauss quickly came up with the formula $\text{sum} = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}$ and found the answer in mere moments. Centuries later, Gauss appears before you in a nightmare with a daunting task...*

You are given a positive integer $n$, find a sequence of integers $[a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n]$ such that $1 \leq a_i \leq 10^{18}$ for all $1 \leq i \leq n$, and the [GCDs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_common_divisor) of pairwise adjacent elements of $a$ are all distinct. Formally,

$\gcd(a_i, a_{i+1}) \neq \gcd(a_j, a_{j+1})$ for each $1 \leq i \lt j \lt n$

Additionally, $a$ should have the **minimum possible** number of distinct elements.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $t$ ($1 \le t \le 200$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first and only line of each test case contains a single integer $n$ ($2 \leq n \leq 5000$) — the size of the sequence to be found.

## Output

For each test case, output $n$ space-separated positive integers $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ ($1 \leq a_i \leq 10^{18}$) on a new line that satisfy the condition in the statement. If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.

It can be proven that under the problem constraints, a solution always exists.

## Note

For the second test case, the GCDs of adjacent elements are $[\gcd(1, 4), \gcd(4, 4), \gcd(4, 6), \gcd(6, 6)] = [1, 4, 2, 6]$, all of which are distinct.

For the third test case, the GCDs of adjacent elements are $[\gcd(4, 4), \gcd(4, 6), \gcd(6, 6), \gcd(6, 9), \gcd(9, 9), \gcd(9, 4)] = [4, 2, 6, 3, 9, 1]$, all of which are distinct.

For each test case, it can be proven that no sequence with fewer distinct elements exists such that all adjacent GCDs are distinct.
statementZhMd:
**这是本题的困难版本。两个版本的区别在于本版本中 $n \leq 5000$。只有当你做出了本题的所有版本时，才可以进行 hack。**

*传说高斯年少时还是个小学生，老师给全班布置了求 $1$ 到 $100$ 的整数之和的任务，大概是为了让学生们能忙活上一阵子。然而，小高斯很快便想出了公式 $\text{sum} = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}$，顷刻之间就得出了答案。几个世纪后，高斯在一场噩梦中出现在你面前，带来了一项艰巨的任务……*

给定一个正整数 $n$，请找出一个整数序列 $[a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n]$，使得对所有 $1 \leq i \leq n$ 都有 $1 \leq a_i \leq 10^{18}$，并且 $a$ 中相邻元素对的 [GCD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_common_divisor)（最大公因数）两两不同。形式化地说，

对每个 $1 \leq i \lt j \lt n$，都有 $\gcd(a_i, a_{i+1}) \neq \gcd(a_j, a_{j+1})$。

此外，$a$ 应当具有**尽可能少的**不同元素个数。

## 输入格式

每个测试包含多个测试用例。第一行包含测试用例的数量 $t$（$1 \le t \le 200$）。接下来是各测试用例的描述。

每个测试用例的第一行也是唯一一行包含一个整数 $n$（$2 \leq n \leq 5000$）——表示要找的序列的大小。

## 输出格式

对于每个测试用例，在新的一行中输出 $n$ 个用空格分隔的正整数 $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$（$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^{18}$），满足题面中的条件。如果存在多组解，输出任意一组即可。

可以证明，在题目约束下解总是存在的。

## 说明

对于第二个测试用例，相邻元素的 GCD 为 $[\gcd(1, 4), \gcd(4, 4), \gcd(4, 6), \gcd(6, 6)] = [1, 4, 2, 6]$，它们两两不同。

对于第三个测试用例，相邻元素的 GCD 为 $[\gcd(4, 4), \gcd(4, 6), \gcd(6, 6), \gcd(6, 9), \gcd(9, 9), \gcd(9, 4)] = [4, 2, 6, 3, 9, 1]$，它们两两不同。

对于每个测试用例，可以证明不存在这样的序列：它的不同元素个数更少，且所有相邻 GCD 两两不同。
